summary: Authored a 5-phase plan (3.25h, waves [1,3,5]/[2]/[4]) finalizing the representation-source acquisition. Research already performed the acquisition itself, so the plan covers what remains: auditing the gehrke_jonsson_2004 registration, earning or downgrading its over-strong verified_conversion fidelity label, recording the seven confirmed-unacquirable sources durably in ~/Projects/Literature/SOURCES.md (the corpus's established W-/A-series blocker format), logging the zotero-cli-cc/httpx2 write-bridge defect in specs/errors.json, and landing a scoped commit of the sub-index.

artifacts.summary: 5-phase implementation plan: registration audit, fidelity spot-check and label reconciliation, durable SOURCES.md blocker record, errors.json defect entry, scoped commit and backup cleanup.

decisions_made: Did not plan a re-run of Tier 3 discovery for the seven unacquired sources: Tier 3 was verified healthy across ~10 queries this session with zero TIER3_STATUS: FAILED, so the rate-limit hypothesis that justified this retry task is discharged and each remaining blocker is now source-specific.

Planned no commit in the ~/Projects/Literature/ repository. Its index.json carries 7,205 insertions across five doc_ids (four belonging to concurrent lamport/wijesekera/xu ingests) and SOURCES.md carries 215 uncommitted lines from another task's dossier; no non-interactive staging can separate them, and git add -p is unavailable. The plan writes to that working tree and requires the summary to name the uncommitted paths.

Verified and rejected three candidate defects before planning around them: the corpus dir's sparse metadata.json (151 of 163 such files are equally sparse — the norm, not a defect), the absence of a full {doc_id}.md (only 132 of 299 source dirs have one), and the per-chunk global-index entries (91 of 164 doc_ids have multiple entries — also the norm).

user_decision.question: Sambin & Vaccaro 1988 'Topology and duality in modal logic' is free-to-read at the publisher (Unpaywall is_oa: true, oa_status: bronze) but ScienceDirect returns HTTP 403 to a non-browser fetch, so it is blocked by an anti-bot/TDM control rather than a paywall. SOURCES.md's policy says 'no paywall circumvention' but also treats anti-bot-walled free items (W11/W13/W16) as the cheapest acquisitions; Playwright is available in this session. Should a browser-driven fetch be authorized for this item?
options: Record it as not acquired (plan Phase 3, entry R1) and leave acquisition to a human with a real browser or institutional access
Authorize a Playwright-driven fetch of the free-to-read publisher copy and ingest it as an eighth source
Authorize a Playwright-driven fetch as a general policy for any Unpaywall-bronze item this pipeline's curl tooling cannot reach
user_decision.recommended: Record it as not acquired (plan Phase 3, entry R1) and leave acquisition to a human with a real browser or institutional access
